recommendation: Keep the source fix. It completes the special-designation removal in the active ModelInfo surface without broadening the change into unrelated legacy MedicinalProduct* ModelInfo cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-25086 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to remove MedicinalProductDefinition.SpecialDesignation because orphan/special designation should be represented through RegulatedAuthorization, with narrower details handled there or by extensions.
initial_application: Commit d017cd22c28c50b2e285e0a2b5dc87edcc6dbb71 explicitly applied GF#25086 by removing the MedicinalProductDefinition.specialDesignation spreadsheet rows. The current MedicinalProductDefinition StructureDefinition no longer contains specialDesignation, and RegulatedAuthorization now carries subject, type, indication, and intendedUse with an Orphan Drug Authorization type code.
additional_context: MedicinalProductDefinition, RegulatedAuthorization, and Library are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. source/library/list-Library-examples.xml and publish.ini keep Library/FHIR-ModelInfo and source/library/library-fhir-model-definition-content.xml in the published build. Neighboring reconciliation commits have treated the FHIR 6.0.0 ModelInfo payload as an active computable surface. Community searches for FHIR-25086 and special-designation terms found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Removed MedicinalProduct.SpecialDesignation and the specialDesignation member from source/library/library-fhir-model-definition-content.xml and refreshed the embedded base64 attachment in source/library/library-fhir-model-definition.xml.
